children: China's daily crude steel output in August fell 3% from the  month before to hit an eight-month low, as some steelmakers scaled down operatiions amid plunging margins.

The world's largest maker of the metal used in construction and manufacturing produced 74.61 million metric tons of steel in August, down 3.7% from a year earlier, the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) said on Tuesday.
That works out at a daily average of 2.41 million tons, the lowest level since December 2025, according to a Reuters' calculation based on the official data.
Several steelmakers prolonged maintenance on equipment or trimmed output last month as steel margins deteriorated amid resilient feedstock prices and subdued steel consumption, analysts said.
An average of around a third of steelmakers operated at a profit in August, versus 39% in July and 66% in the same month in 2025, data from consultancy Mysteel showed.
In the first eight months of 2026, crude steel output totalled 651.85 million tons, an annual decline 3.1%.
